summary: Suffolk County tower of 1918 on Flanders Hill near Riverhead; observers into 1946, closed 1959, removed 1960. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower, 47 ft per NYSFFLA list and Starr list; the register gives 47 ft concrete footings, steel structure, wood steps and landing platforms
facts.status_note: Dismantled and removed in 1960; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the site

staffing.status: Operated by the Conservation Commission until closure in 1959; wardens and observers named in sources from 1932 to 1946

facts.agency: New York State Conservation Commission (Conservation Department)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts places Flanders Hill southwest of Riverhead; NYSFFLA list places it three miles southeast. Left as a disagreement in the story.
NYSFFLA list and Starr list give the tower as 47 ft; the register gives 47 ft concrete footings. The story attributes the 47 ft to the tower, as two sources do.
Register credits the state Conservation Commission with removal in 1960; NYSFFLA list says a local demolition contractor did it. Both agree on the 1960 date.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' confirmed. No source describes what remains at the site or whether it is open; no access level recorded. The 1933 appointment year is inferred from the June 22, 1933 article date. A fall 2026 library hike listing mentions a possible walk to the former tower site, but both fetch tools got 403 and it is not used. A Facebook snippet places the hill in Southampton; unverified, not used. Brief elevation (75 m) matches the register. No corrections to the brief.
